metadata.name: dd
metadata.displayName: dd - Convert and copy files (disk operations)
metadata.description: Convert and copy files (low-level block copy)

installation.note: dd is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: dd reads from an input (file or device) and writes to an output in blocks. It is used for cloning disks, creating disk images, writing ISO to USB, and low-level copying. A wrong output can overwrite data; use with extreme care.
when_to_use: Clone a disk or partition (dd if= of=)
Create or write a disk image (e.g., ISO to USB)
Wipe a device (dd if=/dev/zero of=...) or create swap file

syntax.description: Common operands: if=FILE (input), of=FILE (output), bs=SIZE (block size), count=N (blocks to copy).

options.description: Block size (e.g., 4M, 512); read/write in this size
Copy N blocks (default: until input ends)

examples.title: Clone a disk to an image
examples.command: sudo dd if=/dev/sdb of=backup.img bs=4M status=progress

examples.title: Write ISO to USB
examples.command: sudo dd if=ubuntu.iso of=/dev/sdc bs=4M status=progress
examples.description: Write ISO to USB device (replace /dev/sdc with your USB)

common_pitfalls.description: Writing to the wrong device (e.g., of=/dev/sda instead of /dev/sdc) can destroy the system disk.
common_pitfalls.solution: Confirm output device with lsblk; triple-check before pressing Enter.

related_commands.description: For regular files use cp; dd is for devices/block copy
For file-level copy with progress and resume
